decision: PROMISING, narrowly scoped to teacher-aligned synthetic mask family
facts: Packed binary mask payload averaged 32847 B with exact function outputs.
Continuous Mirror payload averaged 16750 B, 48.97% smaller than packed binary masks; mask agreement ~0.999963 and query NRMSE ~0.00854.
Generic rank-2 logistic factorization used 16755 B (byte-matched) and query NRMSE ~0.04798; mean fit time ~0.712 s per seeded world/task bank.
Rank-2 PCA used 24964 B and query NRMSE ~0.158.
All basis, task codes, mean vectors, metadata, or packed mask bits were included in actual serialized bytes.
Mirror decode is approximately D×R=8192 MAC per task before mask application; same shared mask multiplication work is 524288 elementwise multiplies/task.
interpretation: A shared continuous task-view representation improves the storage-quality frontier over independent packed binary masks on this intentionally Mirror-aligned teacher family. At essentially equal bytes it also outperforms the fixed-step generic logistic factorization in function error, but this may reflect access to the generating coordinates and does not establish a general Mirror advantage.
hypothesis: Supported only as aligned representational feasibility; broad task-mask compression and learned-view claims are not established.
counter_hypothesis: Teacher masks are generated directly from the same rank-2 score basis and codes that Mirror stores; generic logistic fitting receives only thresholded masks and may be optimization-limited at the frozen 250 updates.
limitations: Teacher family is aligned to Mirror rank-2 view
Synthetic mask-only functions on fixed coordinates
No trained SupSup/Piggyback optimization or natural task accuracy
Generic factorization fixed at 250 Adam updates; longer convergence untested
No wall-clock inference benchmark; operation counts are analytical
